excerpt: For $\nu=(n_1,n_2,n_3)\in\mathbb N_0^3$, set $$ |\nu|=n_1+n_2+n_3,\quad \partial^\nu=\partial_{x_1}^{n_1}\partial_{x_2}^{n_2}\partial_{x_3}^{n_3}, \quad G_\nu=\partial^\nu G. $$ Write $\epsilon_j$ for the multi-index with a single $1$ in position $j$, for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$. ::::construction N-C1 | Higher Eisenstein and elliptic sums Version: 1 Uses: [N-D1](#n-d1), [lattice setup](elliptic-functions.md#e-d1). Justification: Absolute convergence and periodicity in [N2](#n2). Origin: literature Cite: [[1, §§3–5]](#ref-krausshar-2001) --- Let $L\subset\mathbb H$ be a full-rank lattice and let $\nu\in\mathbb N_0^3$ satisfy $|\nu|\ge2$. Form $$ E_\nu(L)=\sum_{\lambda\in L^*}G_\nu(\lambda), \qquad \wp_{L,\nu}(q)=\sum_{\lambda\in L}G_\nu(q+\lambda)-E_\nu(L) \quad(q\notin L). $$ :::: ::::proposition N2 | Convergence and periodicity of the higher sums Version: 1 Uses: [N-C1](#n-c1), [F2](foundations.md#f2), the lattice-count estimate in [E1](elliptic-functions.md#e1). Review: pending Formal: none Origin: literature Cite: [[1, §§3–5]](#ref-krausshar-2001) Proof-cite: [[1, §§3–5]](#ref-krausshar-2001) --- For every full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb H$ and every $\nu\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with $|\nu|\ge2$, the Eisenstein series in N-C1 converges absolutely. The defining series for $\wp_{L,\nu}$ converges absolutely and locally uniformly on $\mathbb H\setminus L$. For every $\omega\in L$ and $q\notin L$, $$ \wp_{L,\nu}(q+\omega)=\wp_{L,\nu}(q). $$ :::proof Proof of N2 F2 gives decay $|q|^{-3-|\nu|}$, with exponent at least $5$. The lattice-count estimate from the proof of E1 therefore proves absolute convergence, uniformly on compact sets away from the lattice for the translated sum. Absolute convergence permits reindexing $\lambda\mapsto\lambda+\omega$, which proves periodicity. ::: :::: ::::proposition N1 | Coefficients at the singularity Version: 2 Uses: [N-D1](#n-d1), [N-C1](#n-c1), [N2](#n2), [E1](elliptic-functions.md#e1). Review: pending Formal: none Origin: literature Cite: [[1, §§3–5]](#ref-krausshar-2001) Proof-cite: [[1, §§3–5]](#ref-krausshar-2001) --- Let $L\subset\mathbb H$ be a full-rank lattice and $j\in\{1,2,3\}$. Let $h_j$ be the smooth extension near $0$ of $\wp_{L,j}-G_j$ supplied by E1. For every $\mu\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with $|\mu|\ge1$, $$ \partial^\mu h_j(0)=E_{\mu+\epsilon_j}(L). $$ :::proof Proof of N1 Differentiate the convergent series for $h_j$ from E1 and evaluate at $q=0$. The subtracted constants disappear, leaving $\sum_{\lambda\in L^*}G_{\mu+\epsilon_j}(\lambda)$. This converges absolutely since $|\mu+\epsilon_j|\ge2$. ::: :::: ::::corollary N3 | Parity cancellation Version: 1 Uses: [N-C1](#n-c1), [N2](#n2), [F2](foundations.md#f2). Review: pending Formal: none Origin: derivation --- For every full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb H$ and every $\nu\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with even $|\nu|\ge2$, $$ E_\nu(L)=0. $$ :::proof Proof of N3 By F2, $G_\nu$ is odd when $|\nu|$ is even. The terms at $\lambda$ and $-\lambda$ cancel, and absolute convergence from N2 justifies pairing them. ::: ::::

N3.statement:
For every full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb H$ and every $\nu\in\mathbb N_0^3$ with even $|\nu|\ge2$,
$$
E_\nu(L)=0.

lattice_setup: Fix a full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb H$, written as $$ L=\mathbb Z\omega_0+\mathbb Z\omega_1+\mathbb Z\omega_2+\mathbb Z\omega_3, $$ where the four generators are linearly independent over $\mathbb R$.
